text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 0.86% today as crude oil prices climbed, with Brent crude breaking back above $100 a barrel following reports that Chinese refiners have suspended October fuel exports to protect domestic supplies. This tightening in global fuel availability supports prices for refined products that U.S. refiners like Marathon produce and sell. U.S. refineries are running at 92.5% capacity, so higher oil and product prices flow more directly to the bottom line when utilization is already elevated.

The move also fits into a broader pattern of geopolitical tightness in energy markets — with Iran tensions, questions around LNG project financing, and Trump considering a diesel export ban all adding uncertainty. These supply concerns keep crude prices elevated even as U.S. crude trades well below global benchmarks ($96 versus $114 for Brent), which benefits U.S.-based refiners that can buy cheaper domestic oil and sell products at prices set by global markets.
